finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: if the packet contains maliciously crafted input
finding.assumptions: The packet content is attacker-controlled and the printf function does not sanitize the input properly.

parsed.refutation_attempt: The sink in question is a printf with a string literal format: printf("Received custom header: field1=%u, field2=%u\n", field1, field2). The format string contains no user-controlled data, and the arguments are numeric values parsed from the packet header (field1 and field2). Since no variable format string is used and no packet contents are directly passed to printf as part of the format string, there is no format string vulnerability or command injection path. The only untrusted data is the numeric header fields, which are safely converted to integers before printing.

finding.title: Buffer Overflow
finding.trigger: if the received packet size exceeds 4096 bytes
finding.assumptions: The packet size is not checked before copying it into the fixed-size packet buffer.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Verified that recvfrom is called with the buffer size (sizeof(packet)) as its third argument, ensuring it will not write more than 4096 bytes into the fixed-size packet buffer, thus preventing any buffer overflow.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: if the packet contains maliciously crafted input
finding.assumptions: The packet content is attacker-controlled and the printf function does not sanitize the input properly.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Examined the printf call at line 55: the format string "Received custom header: field1=%u, field2=%u\n" is a compile‑time constant and does not include any %s or %x specifiers that could interpret attacker‑controlled data as a format string. The arguments supplied (field1 and field2) are 16‑ and 32‑bit unsigned integers extracted from the packet, and are printed with %u, which only interprets them as numbers. No conversion of packet data into a format string occurs, and there are no unchecked string operations feeding into printf. Thus the path from the untrusted packet to the sink is fully neutralised by the use of a constant format string and numeric specifiers.

finding.title: Buffer Overflow
finding.trigger: if the received packet size exceeds 4096 bytes
finding.assumptions: The packet size is not checked before copying it into the fixed-size packet buffer.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked the call to recvfrom on line 41. The third argument is sizeof(packet), which equals 4096. This means recvfrom will read at most 4096 bytes, truncating any excess data and preventing overflow of the packet buffer. The buffer itself is declared on line 19 with a fixed size of 4096, and no other memory operations (e.g., memcpy, strcpy) are performed that could overflow it. No unchecked copying or indexing occurs after recvfrom. Therefore the described buffer overflow cannot happen.
